apps.description: Open Android remote for Apple TV over the local network (Companion Link). With an LG webOS TV, one button turns the TV on, picks the Apple TV input and wakes it. No account, no cloud.
apps.releaseNotes:
## What's new

- **More reliable wake-up through the LG TV:** the Wake-on-LAN packet is now repeated before every attempt to reach the TV during the wait, so a TV that misses the first packet still switches on.
- **Power button while connecting:** a tap made while the app is still connecting now waits for that attempt to finish, then puts the TV to sleep if it answered or wakes the chain if it did not. It no longer spends extra seconds re-resolving the TV's address first.
- **Connection log on disk:** the log survives app restarts and covers the whole wake-up chain, every command and every connection change. The log screen has a share button that hands the log files to any app you choose. Typed text is never logged.

## Installing

Download `apple-tv-remote-0.1.5.apk` below and open it on the phone. It installs over 0.1.4 and keeps your pairings. Requires Android 14 (API 34) or newer.

apps.description: A modern open-source Android launcher built with Jetpack Compose and Material 3 — customizable and bilingual (English/Finnish).
apps.releaseNotes:
A small update on top of 0.8.0. Updating keeps your layout, widgets and settings.

**Changed**
- **Backup file name**: *Export to file* now suggests a name with the date and time, for example `ARK-launcher-backup-2026-10-01_08-40.json`. Before, every export offered the same name, so a second backup either replaced the first or got a "(1)" added by the file picker. Older backups import exactly as before.

**Fixed**
- A page that looked empty could not be removed when it still held an item the home screen cannot show — most often an app you have disabled, or a shortcut its app no longer provides. *Remove empty page* now appears for every page that shows nothing, and removing the page clears such leftovers. (This fix first shipped in 0.8.1; it is included here for everyone who updates through an app store.)

No new permissions. Get updates from this page, from [Obtainium](https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium) with this repository as the source, or from the app store you use.

apps.description: Oppiva suomalainen Android-näppäimistö: omat sanat ja ennustus, sanelu, korjausnäkymä, emojit ja paikallinen käännös — oppiminen tapahtuu kokonaan laitteella.
apps.releaseNotes:
## Salasanat ja tunnukset näppäimistön riville

Täyttöpalvelun (esimerkiksi Holvi-salasanasovelluksen) ehdotus näkyy nyt
näppäimistön ehdotusrivillä chipinä sen sijaan, että se putoaisi kentän
viereen. Chip näkyy myös silloin, kun kirjautumiskenttä on jäänyt
näppäimistön alle piiloon, ja se korvaa sanaehdotukset niin kauan kuin
täyttöehdotuksia on. Salasanakentässä rivi näkyy vain chippien kanssa.
Chipin napautus avaa täyttöpalvelun vahvistuksen, ja tunnus ja salasana
täyttyvät kuten ennenkin. Toimii Android 11:stä alkaen; muissa versioissa
mikään ei muutu.

Holvi tarvitsee version 1.1.3, joka ilmoittaa tuen ja antaa ehdotukselleen
näppäimistön rivin esityksen. Chipissä ei näy tunnuksia eikä salasanoja.

## Korkeus vaakasuunnassa ja pienillä näytöillä

Näppäimistön korkeusasetus on nyt pystysuunnan koko. Vaakasuunnassa ja
pienillä näytöillä rivit kutistuvat niin, että työkalurivi, ehdotusrivi,
näppäimet ja navigointipalkki vievät enintään 65 % ikkunasta, samassa
suhteessa kuin Gboard. Pystysuunnassa Pixel-puhelimilla mikään ei muutu:
esimerkiksi 130 % pysyy täsmälleen ennallaan. Aiemmin 130 % peitti
vaakasuunnassa koko ruudun, eikä kenttää nähnyt lainkaan.

---

**Päivitys aiemmasta versiosta:** asenna APK vanhan päälle, data
säilyy. Jos laitteella on kehitysversio (debug), ota ensin
varmuuskopio asetuksista — kehitys- ja julkaisuversio on allekirjoitettu
eri avaimella, joten vaihto vaatii sovelluksen poiston.

apps.description: Android dialer and messaging app that replaces the default Phone and Messages apps - Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Material 3, no internet permission
apps.releaseNotes:
## What's new

Caller announcement no longer goes silent for good after a Speech Services update: when the speech engine's binding dies underneath a long-running app, the app now rebuilds it and speaks the name again (this was eleven days of vibrate-only calls in voice-only announce mode).

Android 17 notification rows now show the handset for call notifications and the speech bubble for message notifications again — Android 17 had started drawing the app's launcher icon on every row, which made a missed call look like a text message.

A conversation opened but never sent no longer leaves an empty row in the conversations list.

The version shown in Settings now names its build (for example 1.27-release).

apps.description: Android app store for open-source apps on GitHub. Developers publish an app by adding the topic "arkstore" to its repository; the store installs and updates APKs straight from GitHub releases.
apps.releaseNotes:
- **Apps under their own names**: the list shows the name an app gives itself, read from its APK, instead of the name of its repository, so that for example `bitwarden/android` is shown as Bitwarden
- **Four more places to get apps from**, each with a switch of its own in the settings: apps released on Codeberg and GitLab with the `arkstore` topic, apps found by searching those two, and the catalogues of IzzyOnDroid and F-Droid. Their apps carry the catalogue's name as a label, show what the catalogue warns about, and are checked against the catalogue's checksum before they are installed
- **Listed once**: an app offered by several places is listed once, from its developer when possible; an installed app stays with the place whose files are signed the way it is, and the details name the other places
- **The version that fits**: from IzzyOnDroid and F-Droid the newest version the device can run is offered, also when the very newest needs a newer Android, and an installed app is offered the newest version signed with its key
- **Quick to start**: the apps of the other catalogues are in the list as soon as the store starts, read from the lists last downloaded
- A beta version shows how often the prereleases have been downloaded and the stable version how often the full releases have
- An app whose signing key has been replaced is no longer taken for one signed otherwise, and a file signed with the key the app has now installs whether or not it carries the history of the keys before it
- One faulty entry no longer costs a whole list its apps, two downloads running at once never write to the same file, and the download notification goes away when the last download is done

Download `ARK-Store-1.4.0.apk` below and open it on your phone to install, or update from inside ARK-Store.

beta.releaseNotes:
Beta version for testing.

- **Material surfaces**: an experiment behind a setting. With it on, the screen and everything on it (the search field, the chips, the buttons, the badges, the cards and the sheets) are drawn as brushed metal lit from above; the graphics processor computes the light, the grain and the bevelled edge for every pixel. Needs Android 13
- **Places**: the chips are always shown, in a tone of their own and with a choice of all places; the chip of a place that is off in the settings turns it on
- **Details**: the details say where an installed app came from (Google Play, F-Droid, Aurora Store, ARK-Store or another app) and whether it is signed with the same key as the version offered here, so that ARK-Store can update it
- **Index**: each file carries the key it is signed with, read from the APK's signing block when every signature scheme agrees; the IzzyOnDroid and F-Droid lists are built again once so that their icons appear
- More room between the search field, the chips and the list, and the search field's background lines up with its outline

Install it from inside ARK-Store with "Show beta versions" turned on, or download `ARK-Store-1.5.0-beta.2.apk` below.

apps.description: Find and track Google Play beta programs for your installed Android apps
apps.releaseNotes:
## What's new

- **Fixed: catalog updates were broken on Android 8-11.** The community
  catalog grew past 1000 apps, which hit a SQLite limit on older Android
  versions and left the catalog frozen or empty on those devices. Catalog
  refresh now works on every supported Android version again.
- **Catalog notes are now translated.** "Confirmed via Google Play",
  "Reported by users" and "Beta build seen on APKMirror" show in all seven
  languages instead of English only.
- **No more false "a beta slot opened" notifications** when Google changes
  the testing-page layout: an unreadable page is now treated as a failed
  check instead of overwriting the last known status.
- **Scans can no longer hang at the very end** of a run — a rare timing issue
  could previously leave the scan notification stuck until the next reboot.
- **Sign-out now removes all scan observations** from the device, including
  ones recorded under an earlier login (privacy improvement).
- **Safer catalog links:** beta testing pages from the shared catalog are
  only ever opened on play.google.com.

Same signing key as every release — installs directly over any previous version.

apps.description: Android device monitor with a home-screen widget, per-app usage insights and a charging screensaver. Fully offline - no internet permission. GPL-3.0-or-later.
apps.releaseNotes:
## What's changed

- **Optional extended access** through **Shizuku** (no root needed) or **root**, under Settings → Extended access. Off by default: nothing is read, no `su` is started and no Shizuku request is made until you switch it on, and the app still has no internet permission.
- With it on, the Home and Device tabs show the **real CPU load** instead of the frequency estimate, **chip temperatures** (CPU, graphics, surface), **graphics load**, and the **battery's health, cycle count, first-use and manufacturing dates** where the phone reports them.
- **Android's own battery statistics** on the since-charge page: drain per hour with the screen on and off, how long a full battery would last at that pace, each app's share, and what kept the phone awake (wake locks and wakeup reasons), explained in plain words (#3).
- Shizuku stops at every reboot: the switch stays on, says it is waiting, and the readings return by themselves once Shizuku is started again. Root that is revoked is given up after three refusals, and the switch says so.
- Phones without a battery charge counter show no drain pace rather than a false zero.

## Using Shizuku

Install [Shizuku](https://shizuku.rikka.app/), start it (wireless debugging on Android 11+, or ADB), then switch **Shizuku** on in Device Watch's Settings and allow the request. The readings are read-only; see PRIVACY.md for what the access covers.

## Installing

Updates cleanly over v1.4.x, v1.5.0 and v1.6.x. If you are coming from v1.3.1 or older (package `com.example.modernwidget`), uninstall the old app first — it is a different package and will not update.
